Project Settings > Plugins > DreamTexture. Saved to the project's Config/DefaultEditor.ini.

Launch arguments passed to dreamtexture.exe, appended to the command line as they are, for example -config followed by the path of a configuration file. If left empty, the backend uses its own default configuration (configs/dreamtexture.json next to the program). Note that the backend's addr must match the Backend URL above; otherwise the process starts but nothing answers at that address, and the plugin only reports an error after it times out.

Path to dreamtexture.exe. The plugin uses it to start the backend. If left empty, the plugin only connects and does not manage the backend: when it cannot connect, the panel shows a hint instead of starting one on its own.
Backend address. The default port matches configs/dreamtexture.json in the backend.
Content root folder that imported assets are placed under.
Initial backoff before reconnecting after a disconnect, in milliseconds. It doubles on every attempt up to Reconnect Max (ms), and resets once connected.
Upper limit of the reconnect backoff, in milliseconds.

How long without receiving any message before the connection is considered dead, in milliseconds. The backend sends a heartbeat text frame every 15 seconds (HeartbeatInterval in internal/api/websocket.go). The default of 40000 is the same value as STALE_AFTER in the web UI: a little more than two beats of margin, so a short scheduling stall does not cut a good connection. Before changing it, read the comment above STALE_AFTER in web/src/store.ts of the DreamTextureDesktop repository: both sides must be changed together.

Automatically import the variants submitted from the Generate page into the project once they finish (the same path as the Import button in the Library). Off by default: you generate several variants to choose from, and importing all of them leaves a pile of assets you do not want. The setting is only checked at the moment a variant finishes and is not applied retroactively: variants that finished while it was off are not imported later if you turn it on.

When the editor starts, if a backend executable is set above and nothing is answering at the backend address yet, start the backend automatically. Off by default: the backend's ComfyUI takes VRAM and the editor needs VRAM too, so it should not be started for someone who has no plans to generate images. When off, the backend is still started on demand, when it is needed (clicking Start Backend, or generating from the Generate page).

After import, automatically create (or update) the material instance MI_<name>, whose parent is the master material M_DreamTexture_Master that the plugin generates under the Import Root folder. When off, only the textures are imported.

Also import the separate channel textures (Roughness, Metallic, Ambient Occlusion) in addition to the packed texture (ORM). Off by default: the ORM texture already covers these three, and the master material only samples the ORM. Turn it on only if you want to hand the textures to another DCC tool.
